full_text_en:
China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd., Dalian Donggang Sub-branch v. Dalian Zhenbang Fluorine Coatings Co., Ltd. and Dalian Zhenbang Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over a loan contract

[Ruling Summary]

Article 16, paragraph 2 of the Company Law of the PRC provides that where a company provides a guarantee to a shareholder or actual controller of the company, it must be resolved by the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders. This provision pertains to the internal control and management of a company and shall not be used as the basis for evaluating the validity of a contract. Where the guarantor argues that the legal representative's act of concluding the mortgage contract exceeded the scope of authority, and the creditor claims, on the ground that it has fulfilled the obligation of formal review of the relevant shareholders' meeting resolution, that the legal representative of the guarantor constituted apparent representation, the People's Court shall uphold such claim.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Judgment

(2012) Min Ti Zi No. 156

Petitioner for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd., Dalian Donggang Sub-branch (formerly China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd., Dalian Shengli Square Sub-branch). Address: No. 28, Shengli Square, Zhongshan District, Dalian, Liaoning Province.

Responsible Person: Xue Xiaodong, Branch Manager.

Agent ad litem: Gao Beigi, Employee of the Bank.

Agent ad litem: Wang Li, Attorney, Liaoning Jinchen Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Dalian Zhenbang Fluorine Coatings Co., Ltd. Address: Yingchengzi Jinlong Temple, Ganjingzi Sub-Park, High-Tech Park, Dalian, Liaoning Province.

Legal Representative: Chen Hengfu, Chairman of the Board.

Defendant at First Instance: Dalian Zhenbang Group Co., Ltd. Address: No. 16, Minyi Street, Zhongshan District, Dalian, Liaoning Province.

Legal Representative: Zhou Jianliang, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Bo, Attorney, Liaoning Junguangze Law Firm.

The petitioner for retrial, China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd., Dalian Donggang Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as CMB Donggang Sub-branch), in the case of dispute over a loan contract with the respondent Dalian Zhenbang Fluorine Coatings Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhenbang Shares Company) and the defendant at first instance Dalian Zhenbang Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhenbang Group Company), disagreed with the civil judgment (2010) Liao Min Er Zhong Zi No. 15 rendered by the Liaoning High People's Court and applied to this Court for retrial. This Court, by civil ruling (2012) Min Shen Zi No. 2 dated July 3, 2012, decided to bring the case for retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with presiding judge Gong Bangyou, judge Zhu Haiyuan, and acting judge Lin Haiquan. The court clerk Lu Yu kept the record. This case is now concluded.

The Dalian Intermediate People's Court found at first instance: On April 30, 2006, CMB Donggang Sub-branch and Zhenbang Group Company entered into a loan contract numbered 2006 Nian Lian Dai Zi No. SL006, stipulating: the loan amount was RMB 14,965,000; the loan term was from April 30, 2006 to June 30, 2006; if the actual date of loan disbursement differed from the above commencement date, the commencement and expiry dates of the loan would be determined by the dates on the loan receipt; the purpose of the loan was debt conversion (new loan to repay old debt); the loan interest rate was 6.435% per annum; if Zhenbang Group Company failed to repay the loan on time, the overdue portion would incur an interest rate increased by 50% from the original rate from the date of default; during the loan period, if the People's Bank of China adjusted the loan interest rate, the relevant provisions of the People's Bank of China on adjustment of loan interest rates would apply.

On June 8, 2006, Zhenbang Shares Company issued an Irrevocable Guarantee Letter numbered 2006 Nian Lian Bao Zi No. SL002, undertaking to assume joint and several guarantee liability for the above loan, with the scope of guarantee including the loan principal, interest, penalty interest, liquidated damages, and all other related costs. The guarantee period was from the effective date of this guarantee letter until two years after the expiry of the loan contract term. On April 30, 2006, CMB Donggang Sub-branch and Zhenbang Shares Company respectively entered into two Mortgage Contracts, which stipulated that the mortgage would be on Zhenbang Shares Company's state-owned land use right of 182,559 square meters located in Guojiagou Village, Yingchengzi Town, Ganjingzi District, Dalian (land certificate number Da Guo Guo Yong 2005 Di 04038) and 17 sets of properties totaling 24,361.09 square meters located at Guantai Street, Ganjingzi District, Dalian. On June 6 of the same year, mortgage registration was completed with the Ganjingzi Sub-bureau of the Dalian Municipal Bureau of Land, Resources and Housing for the land of 182,559 square meters at Yingchengzi Town, Ganjingzi District, Dalian; on June 8 of the same year, mortgage registration was completed with the Dalian Real Estate Registration and Certification Center for the 17 sets of properties totaling 24,361.09 square meters at No. 8, Yingtai Street, Ganjingzi District, Dalian. The scope of guarantee included but was not limited to the loan principal, interest, penalty interest, liquidated damages, damages for loss, and costs of realizing the claim. CMB Donggang Sub-branch was the second mortgagee after the Bank of China.

On June 8, 2006, CMB Donggang Sub-branch, in accordance with the contract, transferred the loan amount of RMB 14,965,000 into the account of Zhenbang Group Company. After the loan matured, Zhenbang Group Company failed to repay the principal and interest.

Zhenbang Shares Company also did not perform the guarantee obligation.

Zhenbang Shares Company had a total of 8 shareholders, namely Zhenbang Group Company, Tianjin Bohai Rim Venture Capital Management Co., Ltd., Zhonglv Industries Co., Ltd., Liaoning Science and Technology Venture Capital Co., Ltd., Taishan Green Industry Co., Ltd., Dalian Science and Technology Venture Capital Fund Co., Ltd., Wang Zhigang, and Zhang Guozhong. One of the shareholders of Zhenbang Shares Company, Dalian Science and Technology Venture Capital Fund Co., Ltd., changed its name from "Dalian Science and Technology Venture Capital Co., Ltd." to the current name "Dalian Science and Technology Venture Capital Fund Co., Ltd." on May 23, 2003. The matter resolved in the Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution was not approved by the shareholders' meeting of Zhenbang Shares Company, nor did Zhenbang Shares Company convene a shareholders' meeting for this matter.

On June 18, 2008, CMB Donggang Sub-branch filed a lawsuit with the Dalian Intermediate People's Court against Zhenbang Group Company and Zhenbang Shares Company, requesting the court to order Zhenbang Group Company to repay the loan principal of RMB 14,965,000 and interest (including overdue interest) up to the date of payment; to order Zhenbang Shares Company to assume joint and several liability for the above debt; and to order the two defendants to bear the litigation costs and preservation fees.

The Dalian Intermediate People's Court held at first instance: The loan contract signed between CMB Donggang Sub-branch and Zhenbang Group Company represented the true intention of both parties and was legal and valid. CMB Donggang Sub-branch disbursed the loan in accordance with the contract, and Zhenbang Group Company should have repaid the loan principal and interest within the agreed term. Its failure to perform the obligation as agreed constituted a breach of contract and should bear liability for breach of contract in accordance with the law. Regarding the validity of the mortgage contract signed between CMB Donggang Sub-branch and Zhenbang Shares Company and the irrevocable guarantee letter issued by Zhenbang Shares Company, since Zhenbang Group Company was a shareholder of Zhenbang Shares Company, and given that the Articles of Association and shareholders' meeting of Zhenbang Shares Company did not grant special authorization for the company to provide a guarantee to its shareholder or actual controller, i.e., Zhenbang Group Company, in accordance with Article 16 of the Company Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Company Law), Zhenbang Shares Company's provision of a guarantee to its shareholder Zhenbang Group Company must be approved by a resolution of the shareholders' meeting of Zhenbang Shares Company. However, the Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution provided by CMB Donggang Sub-branch was an invalid resolution. Therefore, Zhou Jianliang, the legal representative of Zhenbang Shares Company, had no authority to conclude the mortgage contract and the irrevocable guarantee letter at issue. That is, the mortgage contract and the irrevocable guarantee letter at issue were concluded by Zhou Jianliang beyond his authority. CMB Donggang Sub-branch knew or should have known about Zhou Jianliang's conclusion of the mortgage contract and the irrevocable guarantee letter beyond his authority. The reasons are as follows: 1. Although CMB Donggang Sub-branch obtained the Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution, according to Article 16, paragraph 2 of the Company Law, "Where a company provides a guarantee to a shareholder or actual controller of the company, it must be resolved by the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders." CMB Donggang Sub-branch failed to perform its reasonable obligation of formal review in respect of certain obvious defects in the Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution. For example, one of the seals affixed was named "Liaoning Science and Technology Venture Capital Responsibility Company". According to the Company Law, such a name as "Responsibility Company" could not possibly exist. CMB Donggang Sub-branch should have been able to identify this defect through review but failed to do so. During the trial, CMB Donggang Sub-branch also admitted to this negligence. 2. One of the shareholders of Zhenbang Shares Company, Dalian Science and Technology Venture Capital Fund Co., Ltd., had changed its name from "Dalian Science and Technology Venture Capital Co., Ltd." to the current name "Dalian Science and Technology Venture Capital Fund Co., Ltd." in 2003. However, the Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution was formed in 2006. Therefore, the seal affixed on it, named "Dalian Science and Technology Venture Capital Co., Ltd.", was an obsolete old seal. CMB Donggang Sub-branch should have reviewed this but actually did not fulfill its review obligation. 3. According to Article 16, paragraph 3 of the Company Law, "The shareholder mentioned in the preceding paragraph or the shareholder controlled by the actual controller mentioned in the preceding paragraph shall not participate in the voting on the matters mentioned in the preceding paragraph." Zhenbang Group Company, as a shareholder of Zhenbang Shares Company, should not have participated in the voting on this guarantee matter. However, the seal of Zhenbang Group Company was affixed on the Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution. Since the Company Law has clear provisions on this, CMB Donggang Sub-branch should also have reviewed this. As a result, CMB Donggang Sub-branch also failed to fulfill its review obligation. In summary, CMB Donggang Sub-branch could have easily identified the above obvious defects through review, but it failed to perform its due review obligation. Therefore, it can be determined that CMB Donggang Sub-branch knew or should have known that Zhou Jianliang concluded the mortgage contract and the irrevocable guarantee letter beyond his authority. According to Article 11 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the PRC Security Law (hereinafter referred to as the Security Law Interpretation), "If the legal representative or responsible person of a legal person or other organization concludes a guarantee contract beyond their authority, the representative act is valid unless the counterparty knew or should have known that the act exceeded authority." In this case, the mortgage contract and the irrevocable guarantee letter at issue should be deemed invalid. Since Zhenbang Shares Company, as the guarantor, provided CMB Donggang Sub-branch with a Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution that had affixed forged seals of "Tianjin Bohai Rim Venture Capital Management Co., Ltd.", "Zhonglv Industries Co., Ltd.", "Liaoning Science and Technology Venture Capital Responsibility Company", and "Dalian Science and Technology Venture Capital Co., Ltd.", it was clearly at fault for the invalidity of the mortgage contract and the irrevocable guarantee letter. CMB Donggang Sub-branch, as the creditor, was also at fault for failing to fulfill its corresponding review obligation. Therefore, according to Article 7 of the Security Law Interpretation, "If the principal contract is valid but the guarantee contract is invalid, and the creditor is not at fault, the guarantor and the debtor shall bear joint and several compensation liability for the economic losses of the creditor under the principal contract. If both the creditor and the guarantor are at fault, the part of civil liability borne by the guarantor shall not exceed one-half of the portion of the debtor's debt that cannot be satisfied." Zhenbang Shares Company shall bear one-half of the compensation liability for the portion of Zhenbang Group Company's debt that cannot be satisfied.

On December 3, 2009, the court rendered a judgment in accordance with Articles 196, 206, and 207 of the Contract Law, Articles 7 and 11 of the Security Law Interpretation, and Article 16 of the Company Law: 1. Zhenbang Group Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, repay CMB Donggang Sub-branch the loan principal of RMB 14,965,000 and interest (calculated at the annual interest rate of 6.455% from June 8, 2006 to August 8, 2006, and from August 9, 2006 to the effective date of this judgment at the overdue loan interest rate prescribed by the People's Bank of China for the same period). If the obligation is not performed within the period specified in this judgment, the debt for delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC; 2. If Zhenbang Group Company cannot repay the above amount, Zhenbang Shares Company shall bear compensation liability for one-half of the portion that Zhenbang Group Company cannot satisfy; 3. Dismiss CMB Donggang Sub-branch's other claims. Case acceptance fee of RMB 128,690 and property preservation application fee of RMB 5,000, totaling RMB 133,690, shall be borne by Zhenbang Group Company. Appraisal fee of RMB 62,022 shall be borne by Zhenbang Shares Company.

CMB Donggang Sub-branch, dissatisfied with the above first-instance judgment, appealed to the Liaoning High People's Court, stating: 1. The first-instance judgment found unclear facts. The loan guarantee contract signed between CMB Donggang Sub-branch and Zhenbang Shares Company was true and valid. The irrevocable guarantee letter and mortgage contract issued by Zhenbang Shares Company bore the company's seal and the signature of its legal representative, and mortgage registration was duly completed. This shows that Zhenbang Shares Company was fully aware of its obligations and legal liability. Therefore, it can be affirmed that Zhenbang Shares Company's guarantee for Zhenbang Group Company's loan represented its true intention. Hence, CMB Donggang Sub-branch holds a legal mortgage right, which should be protected by law. 2. The first-instance court erred in applying the law. CMB Donggang Sub-branch had no obligation to review the guarantor's Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution, let alone the responsibility and possibility to verify its authenticity. The first instance, relying on Article 16 of the Company Law, determined that CMB Donggang Sub-branch, as a third party, had a statutory review obligation for the Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution at issue. However, it did not apply Article 22 of the Company Law to find that Zhenbang Shares Company failed to exercise the right of revocation within the statutory period regarding the guarantee resolution and therefore should bear legal liability for the validity of the shareholder meeting guarantee resolution. Article 1 of the General Provisions of the Company Law clearly states that the purpose of the law is "to regulate the organization and conduct of companies." It follows that Article 16 of the Company Law is a mandatory provision for the internal conduct of a company and does not impose an obligation or responsibility on third parties outside the company to verify shareholders' resolutions. The conclusion drawn by the first-instance court that it had an obligation to verify the shareholders' resolution was illogical and contrary to the general principle of the Company Law. A company's provision of a guarantee to a shareholder must be approved by the shareholders' meeting, but the company's deliberation and resolution are internal affairs. Especially for limited liability companies, it is difficult for creditors to review the controlling shareholder and actual controller. Article 22 of the Company Law clearly provides that "If the convening procedures or voting methods of the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders, or the contents of the resolution violate laws, administrative regulations, or the company's articles of association, a shareholder may, within 60 days from the date the resolution is made, request the People's Court to revoke it." Since the first-instance court, in the absence of explicit provisions, determined that a third party has an obligation to review the shareholder meeting guarantee resolution, then the shareholders of Zhenbang Shares Company did not exercise the right of revocation within the statutory period regarding the guarantee resolution, so the resolution should be deemed valid. 3. The Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution met the formal review requirements, and there was no subjective fault. The Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution provided by Zhenbang Shares Company bore the company seal and legal person's signature, which satisfied formal review requirements. The consequences of suspected seal forgery by the shareholders of Zhenbang Shares Company should not be borne by CMB Donggang Sub-branch. CMB Donggang Sub-branch requested the second-instance court to amend the judgment in accordance with the law, ordering Zhenbang Shares Company to assume joint and several guarantee liability for Zhenbang Group Company's loan, or to remand the case for retrial.

Zhenbang Shares Company did not submit a written defense but argued during the trial: 1. The guarantee provided by Zhenbang Shares Company was invalid. The Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution submitted by CMB Donggang Sub-branch violated Article 16, paragraph 2 of the Company Law, as it was not approved by the shareholders' meeting of Zhenbang Shares Company, and thus was an invalid resolution. The seal of Zhenbang Group Company, the guaranteed shareholder, was affixed on the so-called Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution of Zhenbang Shares Company provided by CMB Donggang Sub-branch, violating the mandatory provision of Article 16, paragraph 3 of the Company Law that the guaranteed shareholder must abstain from voting. The seals of the other four shareholder units were affixed, of which two were found to be forged through judicial appraisal, and the names of the other two seals did not match the shareholder unit names and were also forged. Subsequently, the four shareholders did not ratify the content of the Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution. Therefore, formally speaking, even if a so-called shareholders' meeting had been convened, the other shareholders present did not agree to the guarantee, let alone a majority approval, so it also violated Article 16, paragraph 3 of the Company Law, and the shareholders' meeting resolution was invalid. Furthermore, CMB Donggang Sub-branch did not provide the minutes of the shareholders' meeting of Zhenbang Shares Company. The other four shareholders all issued statements stating that no shareholders' meeting was held and no resolution approving the guarantee was made, and that the seals of the other shareholders were forged, which further proves that the shareholders' meeting resolution did not exist. 2. CMB Donggang Sub-branch had an obligation to conduct a formal review of the Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution and failed to fulfill that obligation, demonstrating fault. The first-instance court found the Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution invalid, not revoked. Therefore, CMB Donggang Sub-branch's argument that the right of revocation was not exercised within the statutory period was unfounded. 3. CMB Donggang Sub-branch should bear liability for the invalidity of the guarantee. CMB Donggang Sub-branch was clearly at fault for the consequences of the invalid guarantee, as it failed to perform a reasonably prudent formal review. For example, the so-called "Responsibility Company" is not a recognized corporate form under the Company Law. That CMB Donggang Sub-branch failed to identify such an obvious error clearly indicates fault. This Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution also bore the seal of the guaranteed shareholder, which on its face clearly violated Article 16, paragraph 3 of the Company Law, and CMB Donggang Sub-branch should have identified it. The several defects in the shareholders' meeting resolution were formal defects, and CMB Donggang Sub-branch cannot be excused from liability for not knowing the Company Law. Therefore, CMB Donggang Sub-branch failed to fulfill its reasonable review obligation and should bear legal liability for the invalidity of the guarantee. It requested the second-instance court to dismiss the appeal and uphold the original judgment.

Zhenbang Group Company stated during the trial: It agreed with CMB Donggang Sub-branch's appeal arguments and requested the second-instance court to render a judgment in accordance with the law.

The Liaoning High People's Court, in addition to the facts found in the first instance, also found: Upon the application of Zhenbang Shares Company, the first-instance court commissioned Liaoning Deheng Physical Evidence Judicial Appraisal Institute to appraise the two seals of "Tianjin Bohai Rim Venture Capital Management Co., Ltd." and "Zhonglv Industries Co., Ltd." affixed on the Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution. The appraisal opinion was: The seal impression of "Tianjin Bohai Rim Venture Capital Management Co., Ltd." affixed on the Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution was not made by the same seal as the seal impression of "Tianjin Bohai Rim Venture Capital Management Co., Ltd." affixed on the sample 2006 Annual Inspection Report. The seal impression of "Zhonglv Industries Co., Ltd." affixed on the Shareholder Meeting Guarantee Resolution was not made by the same seal as the seal impression of "Zhonglv Industries Co., Ltd." affixed on the sample 2006 Annual Inspection Report.

Facts further found: The query card for enterprise alteration registration provided by the Shenyang Administration for Industry and Commerce recorded that from February 26, 2004 to August 18, 2006, Liaoning Technology Venture Capital Co., Ltd. had not altered its enterprise name. However, the seal affixed on the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution" was that of "Liaoning Technology Venture Capital Liability Company". The query card for alteration of domestic-funded enterprises issued by the High-tech Park Sub-bureau of Dalian Administration for Industry and Commerce recorded that the former Dalian Technology Venture Capital Co., Ltd. had been altered to Dalian Technology Venture Capital Fund Co., Ltd. on May 23, 2003. According to the amendment to the articles of association of Zhenbang Joint Stock Company issued by the High-tech Park Sub-bureau of Dalian Administration for Industry and Commerce on July 22, 2002, the seal affixed by the former shareholder Dalian Technology Venture Capital Co., Ltd. bore numerals, whereas the seal of Dalian Technology Venture Capital Co., Ltd. affixed on the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution" bore no numerals.

Further facts found: Among the eight shareholders of Zhenbang Joint Stock Company, Wang Zhigang and Taishan Green Industry Co., Ltd. did not sign or affix seals on the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution". According to the articles of association of Zhenbang Joint Stock Company, Zhenbang Group Company held 61.5% of the total share capital, and Zhenbang Group Company was a shareholder and the actual controller of Zhenbang Joint Stock Company.

The Liaoning High People's Court held in its trial: The loan contract entered into between CMB Donggang Sub-branch and Zhenbang Group Company was a true expression of intent and was lawful and valid. Zhenbang Group Company failed to perform its obligations under the contract and should bear liability for breach of contract. Zhenbang Joint Stock Company provided joint and several liability guarantee and mortgage guarantee for the loan of Zhenbang Group Company. Since such guarantee act constituted a joint stock company providing guarantee for its shareholder, the determination of its validity should apply the relevant provisions of the Company Law. Article 16, paragraph 2 of the Company Law provides: "Where a company provides a guarantee for its shareholder or actual controller, a resolution of the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders must be adopted." Paragraph 3 provides: "The shareholders specified in the preceding paragraph or the shareholders controlled by the actual controller specified in the preceding paragraph shall not participate in the voting on the matters specified in the preceding paragraph. Such matters shall be adopted by a simple majority of the voting rights held by the other shareholders present at the meeting." Accordingly, as the creditor, CMB Donggang Sub-branch should examine the authenticity of the loan mortgage contract and the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution" and other related materials submitted by the borrower from both procedural and formal aspects. The "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution" bore a total of five seals, and except for the seal of Zhenbang Group Company, none of the seals affixed were genuine. The seals of shareholder Tianjin Bohai Rim Venture Capital Management Co., Ltd. and Zhonglv Industrial Co., Ltd. affixed on the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution" were both determined to be forged by judicial appraisal. The shareholder name was "Liaoning Technology Venture Capital Co., Ltd.", but the seal affixed on the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution" bore the name "Liaoning Technology Venture Capital Liability Company", lacking the word "Co., Ltd." (the Chinese term "youxian" meaning "limited"), which was clearly inconsistent with the shareholder name. Shareholder Dalian Technology Venture Capital Co., Ltd. had already changed its name from "Dalian Technology Venture Capital Co., Ltd." to its current name "Dalian Technology Venture Capital Fund Co., Ltd." in 2003. Although the name on the seal affixed was the former name, it was not the former discarded old seal. Since the old seal of the company before the name change bore a numeral symbol, while the old seal affixed on the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution" bore no numeral symbol, CMB Donggang Sub-branch should have detected this. Furthermore, Zhenbang Group Company, being a shareholder and actual controller of Zhenbang Joint Stock Company, also affixed its company seal on the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution", which violated the provisions of the Company Law, and CMB Donggang Sub-branch should have been aware of this. In summary, all five seals affixed on the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution" were invalid. The first instance judgment correctly found that the matters set forth in the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution" had not been approved by the shareholders' meeting, and the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution" was lacking in authenticity, resulting in the invalidity of the guarantee contract. CMB Donggang Sub-branch failed to fulfill its duty of examination and was at fault, and should bear corresponding liability for the invalidity of the guarantee contract. Pursuant to Article 7 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law: "Where the main contract is valid but the guarantee contract is invalid, if the creditor is not at fault, the guarantor and the debtor shall bear joint and several compensation liability for the economic losses of the creditor under the main contract; if both the creditor and the guarantor are at fault, the portion of civil liability to be borne by the guarantor shall not exceed one-half of the portion of the debt that the debtor cannot repay." In this case, both CMB Donggang Sub-branch and Zhenbang Joint Stock Company were at fault for the invalidity of the guarantee contract. Therefore, the first instance judgment ordering Zhenbang Joint Stock Company to bear one-half of the compensation liability for the portion of Zhenbang Group Company's debt that cannot be repaid was not improper. CMB Donggang Sub-branch's appeal ground that the first instance court erred in applying the law and that it was not at fault could not be established and was not adopted by this court. In conclusion, the facts found in the first instance were clear, the evidence was indeed sufficient, and the trial procedure was lawful, so the first instance judgment should be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court rendered the following judgment: Appeal rejected, and the first instance judgment affirmed. The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 128,690 shall be borne by CMB Donggang Sub-branch.

CMB Donggang Sub-branch, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the Liaoning High People's Court, applied to this court for retrial, alleging: (1) The second instance effective judgment erred in the application of law. This case should apply the provisions of Article 106 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Property Law) regarding the bona fide acquisition system, whereby the applicant for retrial, CMB Donggang Sub-branch, lawfully obtained the mortgage. The applicant for retrial, CMB Donggang Sub-branch, obtained the mortgage over the land involved in the case, which falls under the category of security interests. Pursuant to Article 106 of the Property Law, CMB Donggang Sub-branch bona fide acquired the mortgage over the land and buildings involved in the case. First, CMB Donggang Sub-branch was bona fide when it obtained the mortgage. The setting of the mortgage over the land use rights by Zhenbang Joint Stock Company was for the purpose of borrowing new loans to repay old ones. As a financial institution, the bank's act of providing loans and obtaining mortgages was bona fide and proper. CMB Donggang Sub-branch granted the loan only after the mortgage registration was completed, and there was no malicious purpose whatsoever. Second, while obtaining the mortgage involved in the case, CMB Donggang Sub-branch disbursed the loan to Zhenbang Group Company as contracted, i.e., paid reasonable consideration. Third, mortgage registration had already been established for the real estate mortgage. Pursuant to the Property Law, regardless of whether Zhenbang Joint Stock Company had the authority to register the mortgage over the land involved in the case or whether its shareholders' meeting had consented, this does not affect CMB Donggang Sub-branch's lawful acquisition of the mortgage over the land and buildings involved in the case based on the bona fide acquisition system under the Property Law. The second instance court's judgment, which held that "Zhenbang Joint Stock Company provided joint and several liability guarantee and mortgage guarantee for the loan of Zhenbang Group Company. Since such guarantee act constituted a joint stock company providing guarantee for its shareholder, the determination of its validity should apply the relevant provisions of the Company Law," reflected a misunderstanding and misapplication of the law. The internal procedures for a company to provide a guarantee for its shareholders should indeed be governed by the Company Law, but the validity of a guarantee that has already been registered as a mortgage with a third party should be governed by the Property Law, as this has transcended the scope of the company's internal issues. As can be seen from the provisions of Articles 1, 149, 150, and 153 of the Company Law, the ultra vires infringement by shareholders is an internal liability issue of the company and cannot be invoked against external creditors. Zhenbang Joint Stock Company had already issued an irrevocable guarantee letter and a mortgage contract to CMB Donggang Sub-branch externally, and had completed the mortgage registration with the mortgage registration authorities. The shareholders' meeting resolution of Zhenbang Joint Stock Company is a matter of its internal management. Whether its formal requirements and content were authentic should not be used to oppose the security interest that CMB Donggang Sub-branch had already lawfully established. As for any losses suffered by Zhenbang Joint Stock Company as a result, the relevant responsible persons within the company should bear compensation liability in accordance with the Company Law. Therefore, the second instance effective judgment, which held CMB Donggang Sub-branch's security interest invalid based on the invalidity of Zhenbang Joint Stock Company's internal "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution", constituted an error in the application of law.

(2) The second instance effective judgment erred in the finding of facts. The second instance effective judgment, which held that the applicant for retrial, CMB Donggang Sub-branch, failed to fulfill its duty of formal examination and thus declared the mortgage involved in the case invalid, constituted an error in the finding of facts. First, as a financial institution, when granting a loan, CMB Donggang Sub-branch necessarily requires the borrower to provide a guarantee and first complete the mortgage registration. In this case, Zhenbang Joint Stock Company used land use rights as security to set up a mortgage. CMB Donggang Sub-branch inevitably had to first sign a mortgage contract with it and complete the registration. As a professional institution engaged in financial business, CMB Donggang Sub-branch is neither a professional legal service institution, nor an administration for industry and commerce, nor a mortgage registration authority. The duty of formal examination of the documents for Zhenbang Joint Stock Company's intended setting of security should be borne by the mortgage registration authority. CMB Donggang Sub-branch, relying on the trust in the credibility of the mortgage registration authority, first completed the mortgage registration and then disbursed the loan to the borrower. There was nothing improper in this. The second instance effective judgment, which imposed the above duty of formal examination on CMB Donggang Sub-branch, which is not a professional legal service institution, nor an administration for industry and commerce, nor a mortgage registration authority, and accordingly declared the mortgage invalid, was an unclear finding of facts. Second, as a bona fide third party, CMB Donggang Sub-branch's formal examination of the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution" was limited to "the existence of this document", and it had no duty or capacity to examine its authenticity. The second instance court's judgment, which required CMB Donggang Sub-branch to conduct substantive examination of the document, was an error in the finding of facts. Because: 1. It lacked the capacity to authenticate the seals of shareholders Tianjin Bohai Rim Venture Capital Management Co., Ltd. and Zhonglv Industrial Co., Ltd. affixed on the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution"; 2. As to the seal with the shareholder name "Liaoning Technology Venture Capital Liability Company" on the resolution, the law does not require CMB Donggang Sub-branch, which is a financial institution and not a professional legal institution or administration for industry and commerce, to be thoroughly familiar with the Company Law. Therefore, CMB Donggang Sub-branch had neither the capacity nor the duty to distinguish the company name under the Company Law; 3. As to the seal of "Dalian Venture Capital Co., Ltd." affixed with an old discarded seal on the resolution, CMB Donggang Sub-branch is not the administration for industry and commerce, nor did it have a duty to inquire with the administration for industry and commerce.

(3) CMB Donggang Sub-branch was not at fault, and the guarantor should bear joint and several compensation liability. It was impossible for CMB Donggang Sub-branch to know that the guarantee and mortgage contracts of Zhenbang Joint Stock Company were ultra vires acts by its internal management personnel in violation of the Company Law and without a shareholders' meeting resolution, because Zhenbang Joint Stock Company provided the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution" document, and the mortgage guarantee had been registered after examination by the administrative authority. If there were problems with the mortgage guarantee, the mortgage registration authority would not have completed the mortgage registration after its review. Article 178 of the Property Law provides: "Where the Security Law is inconsistent with the provisions of this Law, this Law shall apply." At the time of the trial of this case, the Property Law had already come into effect. Pursuant to the principle that new laws prevail over old ones, for the trial of the mortgage part of this case, the provisions of the bona fide acquisition system under the Property Law should apply.

In summary, Zhenbang Joint Stock Company, as the guarantor, should bear joint and several compensation liability. The second instance judgment contained unclear findings of facts and indeed erred in the application of law. The applicant requests a judgment to be changed according to law to uphold the correct implementation of the law and protect the lawful rights and interests of CMB Donggang Sub-branch as a bona fide third party.

The respondent, Zhenbang Joint Stock Company, after being served with summons, did not appear in court for the retrial and submitted a written defense opinion stating: First, the bona fide acquisition system does not apply to this case, and the original trial correctly applied the law; second, the applicant failed to exercise reasonable care and attention, and the original trial correctly found the facts; third, the shareholders' meeting resolution was forged, and the guarantee was not approved by the shareholders' meeting. The "Mortgage Contract" and the "Irrevocable Guarantee Letter" are invalid. The applicant was at fault for the invalid result, and the respondent should only bear compensation liability in the corresponding proportion. The respondent requests that the applicant's application for retrial be dismissed.

The defendant in the original trial, Zhenbang Group Co., Ltd., did not submit any defense opinion.

In addition to confirming the facts found in the first and second instance trials, this court also found the following: During the retrial of this case, the applicant for retrial, CMB Donggang Sub-branch, submitted to this court a new piece of evidence, namely, the list of shareholders' meeting members and the signature specimen of Zhenbang Joint Stock Company, to prove that the signatures and seals on the shareholders' meeting resolution provided by Zhenbang Joint Stock Company to CMB Donggang Sub-branch were consistent with the signature and seal specimens provided by it to CMB Donggang Sub-branch.

This court holds that the focus of dispute among the parties in this case is the definition of the liability borne by the guarantor, Zhenbang Joint Stock Company. Since the loan contract involved in the case has been determined to be valid by both the first and second instance courts, and the applicant for retrial does not object to this, this court directly confirms the validity of the loan contract involved in the case. The "Mortgage Contract" and "Irrevocable Guarantee Letter" involved in the case were guarantee acts made by the guarantor, Zhenbang Joint Stock Company, as a guarantee for the debts of its shareholder, Zhenbang Group Company, to the creditor, CMB Donggang Sub-branch. As a company organization and its acts, it should be regulated by the Company Law, and at the same time, its external guarantee acts in the form of contracts are also subject to the constraints of the Contract Law and the Security Law. The determination of the validity of the company guarantee contract involved in the case, since it does not exceed the scope of contract acts between equal commercial entities, should first be evaluated from the perspective of the relevant provisions of the Contract Law. Regarding the validity of a contract, Article 52 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law) provides: "A contract shall be null and void under any of the following circumstances: ... (5) it violates a mandatory provision of any law or administrative regulation." Regarding the term "mandatory" in the aforementioned law, Article 14 of the Interpretation (II) of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Interpretation (II) of the Contract Law) provides the following interpretation: "The term 'mandatory provision' as referred to in Article 52, item (5) of the Contract Law means a provision that is a validity-related mandatory provision." Therefore, the law and relevant judicial interpretations have already clarified that violating a validity-related mandatory provision of laws or administrative regulations is one of the criteria for determining the validity of a contract. As a legal entity different from a natural person, a company's contract acts, while subject to the regulation of the Contract Law, are also subject to the constraints of the Company Law, which is a special law for companies. Article 1 of the Company Law states explicitly: "This Law is enacted for the purposes of regulating the organization and conduct of companies, protecting the lawful rights and interests of companies, shareholders and creditors, maintaining the social and economic order, and promoting the development of the socialist market economy." Article 16, paragraph 2 of the Company Law provides: "Where a company provides a guarantee for its shareholder or actual controller, a resolution of the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders must be adopted." The above provisions of the Company Law have already clarified that their legislative intent is to limit the conduct of company entities and prevent actual controllers or senior management of the company from harming the interests of the company, minority shareholders, or other creditors. Therefore, their substance is an internal control procedure and cannot be used to bind the counterparty to the transaction. Hence, the above provisions should be understood as administrative mandatory provisions (provisions of a regulatory nature). In principle, a contract should not be determined invalid for violating such provisions. Furthermore, if they were treated as validity-related mandatory provisions, it would reduce transaction efficiency and harm transaction security. For instance, when the shareholders' meeting is to be convened, in what form it is to be convened, and who can represent the true will of the shareholders, all exceed the counterparty's ability to judge and control. If the contract were to be declared invalid simply for violating the shareholders' resolution procedure, it would inevitably reduce transaction efficiency and also leave a systemic loophole for companies to dishonestly claim contract invalidity at will by invoking violations of shareholders' resolutions, ultimately harming transaction security. This would not only violate the principle of good faith in commercial conduct but also contradict fairness and justice. Therefore, the first and second instance courts' determination that the matters set forth in the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution" involved in the case had not been approved by the shareholders' meeting of Zhenbang Joint Stock Company, and that Zhenbang Joint Stock Company had not convened a general meeting of shareholders on this matter, and the consequent finding that the irrevocable guarantee letter and mortgage contract were invalid based on Article 16 of the Company Law, constituted an error in the application of law, which this court corrects.

The facts and evidence in this case show that the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution" involved in the case indeed had certain defects, such as false seals of some shareholders, use of the company seal before its alteration, and the situation where the guaranteed shareholder, Zhenbang Group Company, appeared in the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution", which violated the provisions of the Company Law. Whether the acts of Zhou Jianliang, the legal representative of Zhenbang Joint Stock Company, in entering into the mortgage contract and irrevocable guarantee letter beyond his authority constituted apparent representation, and whether CMB Donggang Sub-branch was bona fide, are also key to determining the liability of the guarantor in this case. Article 50 of the Contract Law provides: "Where a legal representative or the responsible person of a legal person or other organization enters into a contract exceeding his authority, the act of representation shall be effective unless the counterparty knows or ought to know that he has exceeded his authority." During the retrial of this case, the new evidence submitted by CMB Donggang Sub-branch to this court showed that the signatures and seals on the shareholders' meeting resolution provided by Zhenbang Joint Stock Company to CMB Donggang Sub-branch were consistent with the signature and seal specimens provided by it to CMB Donggang Sub-branch at the time of the guarantee act. Moreover, the company seal used by Zhenbang Joint Stock Company when providing the guarantee to CMB Donggang Sub-branch was genuine, and it also bore the genuine signature of its legal representative. Furthermore, the mortgage guarantee involved in the case had been registered after examination by the administrative authority. At this point, CMB Donggang Sub-branch's duty of examination in the process of accepting the guarantee act from the guarantor had been completed, and it had reason to believe in the authenticity of the representation acts of Zhou Jianliang himself as the legal representative of the guaranteeing company. The related defects in the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution" could only be identified through appraisal by an appraisal authority, could only be known through inquiry into the company's business registration, and could only be avoided by being thoroughly familiar with the relevant norms of the Company Law to prevent risks arising from the guarantor company's poor internal management. If all of this were to be attributed to the duty of examination of the guaranteed creditor, it would be excessively harsh and would also contravene the original legislative intent of the Contract Law, the Security Law, and other laws to protect transaction security. The guaranteed creditor, based on its reliance on the identity of the legal representative of the guarantor and the authenticity of the company's legal person seal, and based on the fact that the shareholders' meeting guarantee resolution provided by the guarantor bore the genuine seal of the guarantor company, had full reason to believe in the authenticity of the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution" and had no need and could not possibly further verify the authenticity of the "Shareholders' Meeting Guarantee Resolution" provided by the guarantor. Therefore, in the process of accepting the guarantee provided by Zhenbang Joint Stock Company, a non-listed company, for its shareholder, CMB Donggang Sub-branch had fulfilled its reasonable duty of examination and was subjectively bona fide. The acts of Zhou Jianliang in this case constituted apparent representation, and Zhenbang Joint Stock Company should bear the guarantee liability for the guarantee contract involved in the case.

Regarding the guarantee liability under the "Mortgage Contract" involved in the case, since during the first and second instance trials, CMB Donggang Sub-branch only advanced the claim that the counterparty should bear joint and several compensation liability, and did not advance a request for the right of priority to be satisfied from the mortgaged property involved in the case, its claim in the retrial for the right of mortgage security over the property involved in the case has exceeded the scope of the claims in the original trial. Therefore, this court will not try this matter in the retrial.

In summary, pursuant to Article 50 and Article 52, item (5) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 14 of the Interpretation (II) of the Supreme People's Court on Certain Issues Concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 16, paragraph 2 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 170, paragraph 1, item (2) and Article 207 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court renders the following judgment:

1. The civil judgment (2010) Liao Min Er Zhong Zi No. 15 of the Liaoning High People's Court and items (2) and (3) of the civil judgment (2009) Da Min San Chu Zi No. 36 of the Dalian Intermediate People's Court are hereby reversed;

2. Item (1) of the civil judgment (2009) Da Min San Chu Zi No. 36 of the Dalian Intermediate People's Court is hereby affirmed;

3. Zhenbang Joint Stock Company shall bear joint and several guarantee liability for the above-mentioned debts of Zhenbang Group Company.

If the obligations are not performed within the period specified in this judgment, the debt interest during the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with the provisions of Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 128,690, plus the property preservation application fee of RMB 5,000, totaling RMB 133,690, shall be borne by Zhenbang Group Company. The appraisal fee of RMB 62,022 shall be borne by Zhenbang Joint Stock Company. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 128,690 shall be borne by Zhenbang Joint Stock Company.

This judgment is final.
